title: Taming Wild Knots with Mosaics
summary: Wild knots--knots with infinite knotting behavior--have resisted traditional methods of knot classification, making them more of a curiosity in topology than a subject of sustained investigation. In this paper, we present a new way to investigate these objects. We extend Lomonaco and Kauffman's knot mosaic theory to represent a substantial subclass of wild knots that have isolated wild points. Our mosaics consist of infinite rooted trees with mosaics assigned to vertices and embedding functions governing connections. In developing this framework, we also introduce a notion of mosaic tangles…
